children: Shipping stocks are benefiting from a sharp shift in global freight markets as Middle East tensions disrupt normal trade flows. A group of 35 U.S. and European-listed shipping companies has gained about 68% this year.

Danaos (DAC) has climbed about 60% in 2026 and reached price levels not seen since 2008. Frontline (FRO) and Teekay Tankers (TNK) have moved to their strongest levels since 2011, while BW LPG (BWLP) has reached a record.

Tanker operators have delivered the largest advances, with crude-shipping shares rising about 120% year to date. Longer voyages are also supporting demand across gas carriers, vehicle transporters and dry-bulk fleets as vessels spend more time at sea.
International Seaways (INSW) also recently set a new high. The gains reflect tighter vessel supply and higher freight requirements as ships take longer routes around regional disruptions.
Shipping shares could remain supported while disruptions keep vessels occupied for longer and freight capacity constrained.

title: Shipping Stocks Soar as Hormuz Disruption Sends Tanker Shares Surging
